version.changelog: 1.4.2: bounded-memory pack/unpack SLOs, 5000-file packages, remote-search telemetry gates

llm.summary: This benchmark skill is resource-heavy but its risky actions are disclosed, purpose-aligned, and gated rather than hidden or deceptive.

dimensions.detail: Manual benchmarks can consume hours and tens of GiB, but the skill documents this and the helper requires an explicit --yes flag for the large run.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager hook, remote payload fetch, or auto-run install behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The frontmatter declares only python while the instructions also describe repository inspection, edits, test commands, and cleanup commands, but those are openly documented and normal for this workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, scheduled task, credential activation, shell wrapping, tool hijacking, or hidden background worker was found; the skill explicitly says not to connect credentials or cloud services.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is CloudArc benchmark, SLO, telemetry, and CI support; the artifact contents match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a CloudArc development repository where running tests, writing benchmark reports, and consuming large temporary disk are acceptable. Avoid the manual benchmark unless you intentionally want the large 1/5/10 GiB run, and review cleanup commands before running them in an unusual working directory.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Repository reads/writes and command execution are expected for benchmark and CI work; the only real issue is metadata under-specification, not hidden authority.
[EA2] expected: The cited text is a safety instruction to check skipped files, not evidence of autonomous destructive decisions.
[AST4] expected: The helper uses subprocess.run with explicit argument lists and does not invoke a shell; this is appropriate for running benchmark/test commands.
[TT2] expected: The reviewed code renders a fixed-format SVG badge from parsed benchmark JSON and writes only to a user-specified output path; it is not arbitrary stdin-to-file execution.
[SQP-2] expected: The recursive deletion example is limited to __pycache__ cleanup; it would benefit from an adjacent caution, but it is disclosed and low-impact.
